newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's legislature elections set for July 20.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's legislature elections set for July 20.

text.p: National elections of deputies for the next five-year term of Vietnam's National Assembly will be held on July 20, the official Vietnam News Agency said on Sunday.
VNA said a 21-member central electoral council had been set up ahead of the vote for the 10th legislature's 450 seats, with National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh as its president.

The ninth National Assembly, which is in the middle of its final session, last week adopted revisions to the 1992 law on election of deputies which are expected to bolster the body's role in the national administration.
Among the revisions were an increase in the maximum number of deputies to 450 from 400 and eligibility for assembly candidates to campaign in newspapers and on radio and television.

National Assembly Office Director Vu Mao told reporters last month that non-members of the ruling Communist Party would have a greater voice after the elections in order to make the legislature a more democratic body.

He said the ratio of non-party lawmakers should be raised to 20 percent from about eight percent through the vote. However, he did not explain how -- if the vote was free and fair -- targets could be set for the composition of the assembly.
The tenure of Vietnam's president, currently 76-year-old Le Duc Anh, will end when the ninth legislature is replaced.
Analysts expect Anh, who suffered a stroke late last year, to be replaced after the first session of the new assembly in September or October.
Anh is one of the country's leadership triumvirate with Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi, 80, and Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, 74.
